statement: The full normalizers of the two standard negative torus involutions' Klein-four centralizers are the same explicitly realized geometric D8. This D8 is self-normalizing in the full peripheral outer group and has full centralizer its order-two center. The only finite subgroups containing the specified standard two-section negative involution b0 are its C2, its exact Klein-four centralizer, and that D8. Thus it has a unique maximal finite overgroup; exact conjugation transports the entire list to its known conjugacy orbit.
depends_on: D64 and D65 full standard negative centralizers; D54 nontrivial mod-two homology of cubic elements; D55 the exhaustive nine realized finite torus types and positive quartic square; D56 positivity of the cyclic-six involution; A13 discrete torus peripheral identification; the actual word and homology maps proved here
manuscript_passages: Section 30, folios 194-196, scans 383-387; Section 31, folios 198-199 verso, scans 391-394; Part D(b), full loop-outer finite actions in type (1,1)
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None. The quarter-turn and reflection are specified as actual free-group automorphisms, every inner adjustment to the cusp-normalized representatives is written, and the complete overgroup comparison uses the actual full primary homology map.
notes: Conjugation on either computed Klein group fixes its unique nontrivial multiplier-one element, so its full normalizer has quotient of order at most two and kernel exactly that Klein group. The quarter-turn realizes the exchange in both groups. The first Klein group is the exact kernel of the mod-two homology map on this D8, so the full D8 normalizer also preserves it. In any finite S3 or D12 containing a negative involution, that involution inverts a cubic element. The standard b0 has identity mod-two matrix, whereas every cubic element has exact order three there, giving an immediate contradiction. The remaining V4 and D8 overgroups are forced to be the exact computed groups. This does not establish conjugacy of arbitrary negative involutions or solve the remaining cubic/quartic scalar multiplier cases.
computational_checks: code/part_c/standard_negative_overgroups_d67.py and adjacent JSON/stdout check exact free-word identities, all signed-permutation automorphism products, finite subgroup labels, and all order-three matrix inversion relations in GL2(F2).
